cards.back: to give up; to submit; to state
cards.example: Je moet je naam en adres opgeven.
cards.forms: geeft op · gaf op · heeft opgegeven
cards.note: Can mean quit, provide information, or register oneself.

cards.back: to spend; to publish; to issue
cards.example: De overheid geeft nieuwe paspoorten uit.
cards.forms: geeft uit · gaf uit · heeft uitgegeven
cards.note: Used for money, publications and officially issued items.

cards.back: to display; to reproduce; to represent
cards.example: De grafiek geeft de resultaten duidelijk weer.
cards.forms: geeft weer · gaf weer · heeft weergegeven
cards.note: Frequent in technical, academic and formal contexts.

cards.back: to find; to think; to consider
cards.example: Ik vind dit een goede oplossing.
cards.forms: vindt · vond · heeft gevonden
cards.note: Very common both for locating something and expressing an opinion.

cards.back: to be located; to find oneself
cards.example: Het station bevindt zich aan de andere kant van het plein.
cards.forms: bevindt · bevond · heeft bevonden
cards.note: Usually reflexive: zich bevinden.

cards.example: Veel reizigers ondervonden hinder door de staking.
cards.forms: ondervindt · ondervond · heeft ondervonden
cards.note: Common with effects, difficulties, support and consequences.

cards.example: Ik kon het document nergens terugvinden.
cards.forms: vindt terug · vond terug · heeft teruggevonden
cards.note: Also figurative: zich terugvinden in something = identify with it.

cards.example: Wetenschappers proberen een nieuwe methode uit te vinden.
cards.forms: vindt uit · vond uit · heeft uitgevonden
cards.note: For inventions and discovering an answer through investigation.

cards.example: De vergadering vindt morgen plaats.
cards.forms: vindt plaats · vond plaats · heeft plaatsgevonden
cards.note: A highly frequent fixed verb used for events.

cards.back: to approve; to be okay with
cards.example: Vind je het goed als ik iets later kom?
cards.forms: vindt goed · vond goed · heeft goedgevonden
cards.note: Often appears as vind je het goed als…?

cards.example: Zij spreekt vloeiend Nederlands.
cards.forms: spreekt · sprak · heeft gesproken
cards.note: A common irregular verb.

cards.back: to agree; to arrange to meet
cards.example: We hebben afgesproken om acht uur bij het station.
cards.forms: spreekt af · sprak af · heeft afgesproken
cards.note: Can mean making an appointment or reaching an agreement.

cards.back: to address; to appeal to; to hold accountable
cards.example: De nieuwe campagne spreekt jongeren aan.
cards.forms: spreekt aan · sprak aan · heeft aangesproken
cards.note: Used for speaking to someone, appealing to someone, or confronting conduct.

cards.example: We bespreken het voorstel tijdens de vergadering.
cards.forms: bespreekt · besprak · heeft besproken
cards.note: A central verb in work and study contexts.

cards.example: De getuige sprak de verklaring van de verdachte tegen.
cards.forms: spreekt tegen · sprak tegen · heeft tegengesproken
cards.note: Used when statements or evidence conflict.

cards.back: to pronounce; to express; to declare
cards.example: De minister sprak zijn steun voor het plan uit.
cards.forms: spreekt uit · sprak uit · heeft uitgesproken
cards.note: Can concern pronunciation, opinions, support or official judgments.

cards.back: to address; to speak to an audience
cards.example: De burgemeester sprak de aanwezigen toe.
cards.forms: spreekt toe · sprak toe · heeft toegesproken
cards.note: Usually involves speaking formally to a group or person.

cards.example: Ik denk dat hij morgen komt.
cards.forms: denkt · dacht · heeft gedacht
cards.note: A very common irregular verb.

cards.back: to think of; to invent; to realize
cards.example: We moeten snel een oplossing bedenken.
cards.forms: bedenkt · bedacht · heeft bedacht
cards.note: Zich bedenken means to change one’s mind.

cards.example: Ik wil eerst even over het voorstel nadenken.
cards.forms: denkt na · dacht na · heeft nagedacht
cards.note: Usually used with over.

cards.back: to think along; to help develop ideas
cards.example: De gemeente vraagt bewoners om mee te denken over het plan.
cards.forms: denkt mee · dacht mee · heeft meegedacht
cards.note: A common Dutch concept in collaborative work and decision-making.

cards.example: Ze nam de tijd om haar beslissing te overdenken.
cards.forms: overdenkt · overdacht · heeft overdacht
cards.note: More formal and deliberate than nadenken.

cards.example: Elk jaar herdenken we de slachtoffers van de oorlog.
cards.forms: herdenkt · herdacht · heeft herdacht
cards.note: Used for solemn remembrance of people or historical events.

stellen.coreMeaning: to put, place, set, state, or establish
stellen.pattern: The root often expresses putting something into a position, presenting an idea, or determining a fact. Prefixes narrow the direction or result; many forms are separable.
stellen.memoryHook: Think “set or place.” The prefix tells you what is being set forward, fixed, together, or at ease.
stellen.usageNotes: Watch separability: ik stel het voor, but omdat ik het voorstel. Learn fixed combinations such as een vraag stellen and op prijs stellen.
commonPitfalls: voorstellen can mean propose, introduce, or imagine depending on construction
teleurstellen and geruststellen are inseparable despite looking prefixed

nemen.pattern: Prefixes specify the type or direction of taking: accept, take away, take over, include, consume, or undertake.
nemen.memoryHook: Ask: what is being taken, and in which direction?
nemen.usageNotes: Strong verb: neemt · nam · heeft genomen. Many compounds are separable.
commonPitfalls: aannemen can mean accept, assume, or hire
opnemen has several common senses: record, include, admit, and pick up

zetten.coreMeaning: to put, set, place, or switch
zetten.pattern: Zetten usually describes an active action that moves something into a position or changes its state. Prefixes describe the target or result.
zetten.memoryHook: Zetten is the action; staan is often the resulting position.
zetten.usageNotes: Weak verb: zet · zette · heeft gezet. Many compounds are separable.
commonPitfalls: use zetten for placing something, but staan for where it is
omzetten may mean convert, translate, or generate turnover

houden.coreMeaning: to hold, keep, maintain, or like
houden.pattern: The family develops from holding something in place: retain, stop, maintain, endure, contain, or keep to an agreement.
houden.memoryHook: Picture keeping something in your hands or in the same condition.
houden.usageNotes: Strong verb: houdt · hield · heeft gehouden. Learn fixed prepositions such as houden van and rekening houden met.
commonPitfalls: houden van means to love or like, not literally hold from
ophouden can mean stop, cease, or hold up

brengen.pattern: Prefixes describe where something is brought or the state or result it causes.
brengen.memoryHook: Follow the movement: mee is along, terug is back, over is across.
brengen.usageNotes: Irregular: brengt · bracht · heeft gebracht. Many compounds are separable.
commonPitfalls: uitbrengen has several senses: publish, release, issue, or cast a vote
overbrengen can mean transfer, transmit, or convey

komen.coreMeaning: to come, arrive, happen, or result
komen.pattern: Prefixes describe direction, arrival, occurrence, accessibility, or reaching a result.
komen.memoryHook: Imagine movement toward a place, person, event, or outcome.
komen.usageNotes: Strong verb: komt · kwam · is gekomen. Most motion senses use zijn in the perfect.
commonPitfalls: voorkomen can mean prevent or occur/look familiar, with different stress and separability
overkomen may mean happen to someone or come across as

gaan.coreMeaning: to go, proceed, function, or concern
gaan.pattern: Prefixes turn basic movement into continuation, approach, handling, transition, or participation.
gaan.memoryHook: Start with movement, then let the prefix show the route or purpose.
gaan.usageNotes: Irregular: gaat · ging · is gegaan. Learn fixed prepositions such as omgaan met and ingaan op.
commonPitfalls: aangaan can mean enter into, concern, or switch on
doorgaan can mean continue or take place

maken.coreMeaning: to make, do, create, or cause
maken.pattern: This productive family describes producing, preparing, completing, experiencing, and changing states.
maken.memoryHook: Something is being made into a new result.
maken.usageNotes: Weak verb: maakt · maakte · heeft gemaakt. Many compounds are separable.
commonPitfalls: meemaken means experience, not make along
uitmaken has several meanings, including matter, determine, and break up

trekken.coreMeaning: to pull, draw, move, or attract
trekken.pattern: Meanings grow from physical pulling: attract, withdraw, involve, depart, deduct, or draw a conclusion.
trekken.memoryHook: Picture a force pulling something toward, away, through, or apart.
trekken.usageNotes: Strong verb: trekt · trok · heeft getrokken. Motion uses may take zijn when a destination is emphasized.
commonPitfalls: betrekken can mean involve, occupy, or obtain from a supplier
aftrekken can mean subtract or pull off

vallen.coreMeaning: to fall, occur, or turn out
vallen.pattern: The family covers literal falling, unexpected events, reactions, classifications, and evaluations.
vallen.memoryHook: Something drops into a place, category, or outcome.
vallen.usageNotes: Strong verb: valt · viel · is gevallen. Most literal and change-of-state uses take zijn.
commonPitfalls: meevallen means turn out better than expected
opvallen means stand out or be noticed

lopen.coreMeaning: to walk, run, proceed, or operate
lopen.pattern: Prefixes describe route, duration, process, result, or missed opportunity.
lopen.memoryHook: Imagine a path: along, through, away, behind, or into something.
lopen.usageNotes: Strong verb: loopt · liep · heeft/is gelopen. The auxiliary depends on whether destination/change is emphasized.
commonPitfalls: aflopen may mean end, expire, or walk down
misgelopen means missed or failed to obtain

staan.coreMeaning: to stand, be situated, remain, or allow
staan.pattern: The family describes position, existence, endurance, permission, opposition, and reputation.
staan.memoryHook: Think of something standing in a position or condition.
staan.usageNotes: Strong verb: staat · stond · heeft gestaan. Contrast active zetten with positional staan.
commonPitfalls: toestaan means allow and is not separable
bestaan can mean exist or consist of

geven.coreMeaning: At its core, geven means to transfer, provide, produce, or cause something to be available to someone or something.
geven.pattern: The prefix shows the direction or result of the transfer: aangeven points something out or reports it; doorgeven passes it onward; meegeven sends it along; opgeven gives it up or states it; uitgeven releases or spends it; weergeven presents it again in words, images, or data.
geven.memoryHook: Picture something moving from a giver toward a receiver. The prefix tells you where it goes or what happens to it.
geven.usageNotes: Strong verb: geeft · gaf · heeft gegeven. Many compounds are separable, but their meanings are often idiomatic and must be learned with collocations.
commonPitfalls: aangeven can mean indicate, report, or hand over depending on context
opgeven can mean give up, state, register, assign, or report
uitgeven may mean spend money, publish, or issue

vinden.coreMeaning: At its core, vinden means to discover, locate, judge, or experience something as having a certain quality.
vinden.pattern: The family extends from physically finding something to mentally judging it, locating oneself, experiencing effects, retrieving something, inventing something, or describing an event that takes place.
vinden.memoryHook: Think: “I come upon it” — either in the world, in my thoughts, or in my experience.
vinden.usageNotes: Strong verb: vindt · vond · heeft gevonden. The construction iets + adjective + vinden expresses an opinion: Ik vind het belangrijk.
commonPitfalls: uitvinden means invent or figure out, not simply find outside
plaatsvinden is inseparable and means take place
zich bevinden is reflexive and usually describes location or condition

spreken.coreMeaning: At its core, spreken means to use speech to communicate, discuss, address, pronounce, or reach an agreement.
spreken.pattern: The prefix directs the speech: af- arranges or agrees; aan- addresses or appeals to; be- discusses; tegen- contradicts; uit- pronounces or expresses; toe- addresses an audience.
spreken.memoryHook: Picture speech aimed in a direction. The prefix tells you who receives it or what the speech accomplishes.
spreken.usageNotes: Strong verb: spreekt · sprak · heeft gesproken. Learn fixed combinations such as spreken met, spreken over, iemand aanspreken, and met iemand afspreken.
commonPitfalls: afspreken means arrange or agree, not “speak off”
aanspreken may mean address someone, appeal to someone, or hold someone accountable
uitspreken can mean pronounce, express, or formally deliver

denken.coreMeaning: At its core, denken means to form thoughts, opinions, plans, expectations, or memories in the mind.
denken.pattern: Particles direct the movement of thought: aan points thought toward someone or something; na means reflect further; mee means contribute ideas; over means consider thoroughly; be- often means think up or reconsider; her- means commemorate.
denken.memoryHook: Imagine thought moving in a direction: toward, back over, along with others, or into a new idea.
denken.usageNotes: Irregular verb: denkt · dacht · heeft gedacht. Learn the fixed combinations denken aan, denken over, nadenken over, and meedenken met.
commonPitfalls: denken aan means have someone or something in mind, while denken over means have an opinion about
bedenken can mean devise, think of, or change one’s mind
herdenken means commemorate, not ordinary remembering
